name: Keyed Sort Refreshes Only The Shifted Window

atomicDiscipline.rule: Run exactly the printed hypothesis. If the attempted change fails, degrades, or suggests a different fix, revert to the checkpoint and finish this experiment as failure. Start a new experiment for the next idea.

primaryTarget: native release build, criterion benches (macOS arm64)
hypothesisMarkdown:
## Keyed Sort Refreshes Only The Shifted Window Hypothesis

### Hypothesis

`CacheSortState` handles an update/refresh/move by removing the entry from `sorted` (rewriting `sorted_positions` for every later entry, with a key clone and hash insert each) and re-inserting it (rewriting every later entry again): ~2·(n−i) hash writes per update, which makes `sort-and-page/update` 132 µs at 10k rows. Removing without refreshing and, after the re-insert, refreshing only the entries between the old and new positions gives the same positions with O(|i−j|) cheaper `get_mut` writes.

### Scope Lock

**Tested mechanism:** take-then-reinsert with a single refresh of the shifted window.
**Allowed changes:** `crates/src/collections/operators/cache_sort_state_impl.rs`: new `take_sorted_key`/`insert_taken_entry` and the six update/refresh/move call sites.
**Forbidden in this experiment:** replacing the sorted Vec or position map structure, the Remove/Add paths, paging/diff code.
measurementPlanMarkdown:
### Measurement Plan

Focused tests: `collections::tests::{keyed_sort_positions,sorting_windowing,window_responses,subset_operator_indexes,index_contract_harness,snapshot_diff_indexes,operator_bookkeeping_costs}` (debug_assert_positions checks the map in debug builds); clippy/fmt. Bench `sort_and_page`, `keyed_sort`, `hot_paths` vs base. Pass: sort-and-page/update/10000 >=2x faster.
expectedOutcomeMarkdown:
### Expected Outcome

sort-and-page/update/10000 from ~130 us to tens of us (remaining: Vec memmove and O(distance) position writes).
